q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC), the dedicated financing arm of Indian Railways, was set up in the year:
e: IRFC, the dedicated market-borrowing and financing arm of Indian Railways, was incorporated on 12 December 1986 to raise funds for rolling stock and infrastructure.

q: In the equity of the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), the share held by the Central Government through the Ministry of Railways is:
e: In NHSRCL, the Central Government through the Ministry of Railways holds 50 per cent equity, while Gujarat and Maharashtra hold 25 per cent each for the bullet train project.

q: The Container Corporation of India Limited (CONCOR) was incorporated in the year:
e: CONCOR, the container logistics PSU operating inland container depots and container trains, was incorporated in March 1988 and took over the existing container depots of Indian Railways.

q: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project is being financed mainly through a soft loan from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), which covers about what share of the project cost?
e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project is funded mainly by a JICA soft loan covering about 81 per cent of the project cost, with the balance shared by the Centre and the two states.

q: The Central Organisation for Railway Electrification (CORE) was set up as a centralised organisation for railway electrification projects in the year:
e: CORE, the Central Organisation for Railway Electrification headquartered at Prayagraj, was set up in 1979 to execute railway electrification works on a centralised, turnkey basis.

q: The 'RailOne' super app of Indian Railways, launched in July 2025, was conceived and developed by:
e: RailOne, the all-in-one super app launched in July 2025 for ticketing, enquiry and other passenger services, was conceived and developed by CRIS, the IT arm of Indian Railways.

q: In the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL), the equity share held by the Government of India is:
e: In Konkan Railway Corporation Limited, the Government of India holds 51 per cent equity, with Maharashtra, Karnataka, Goa and Kerala holding the remaining shares.

q: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC), which implements the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridors, was formally incorporated in the year:
e: NCRTC, the joint venture of the Centre and the Delhi, UP, Haryana and Rajasthan governments implementing the RRTS corridors, was incorporated on 21 August 2013.

q: India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper trainset, unveiled in September 2024, was designed and manufactured by:
e: India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper trainset, unveiled in September 2024 for long-distance overnight travel, was designed and manufactured by BEML Limited at Bengaluru.

q: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) was incorporated in the year:
e: IRCTC, which handles online ticketing, catering and tourism for Indian Railways, was incorporated on 27 September 1999 as a PSU under the Ministry of Railways.

q: The Operation Control Centre (OCC) of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor, from where the entire corridor's train operations are monitored, is located at:
e: The Operation Control Centre of the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor, which monitors train operations over the whole corridor, is located at Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh.

q: RITES Limited was granted the 'Navratna' status in October 2023, becoming which numbered Navratna company among the Central Public Sector Enterprises?
e: PIB records that IRCON and RITES were announced as the 15th and 16th Navratna CPSEs respectively in October 2023, so RITES became the 16th Navratna company.

q: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), the project-executing company of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: RVNL, set up to execute rail infrastructure projects such as new lines, doubling and electrification on a fast-track basis, was incorporated on 24 January 2003.

q: The Southern Railway was formed in April 1951 by the merger of which of the following railways?

options.A: Madras Railway, Bengal Nagpur Railway and Mysore State Railway
options.B: Madras and Southern Mahratta Railway, South Indian Railway and Mysore State Railway
options.C: South Indian Railway, Nizam's State Railway and Mysore State Railway
options.D: Madras and Southern Mahratta Railway, South Indian Railway and Scindia State Railway

e: Southern Railway was formed on 14 April 1951 by integrating the Madras and Southern Mahratta Railway, the South Indian Railway and the Mysore State Railway.

q: The first 1,500 V DC electric locomotive turned out by Chittaranjan Locomotive Works, commissioned in October 1961, was named:
e: CLW's first 1,500 V DC electric locomotive, the WCM-5 turned out in 1961, was commissioned by Prime Minister Nehru on 14 October 1961 and named Lokmanya.

q: The Patiala Locomotive Works at Patiala was set up in 1981 under the original name of:
e: The Patiala unit was set up in 1981 as the Diesel Component Works (DCW) to manufacture diesel locomotive components; it was later renamed DMW and then Patiala Locomotive Works.

q: The Modern Coach Factory at Raebareli was earlier known by the name of:
e: The Raebareli coach plant was first set up as the Rail Coach Factory, Raebareli, and was later renamed the Modern Coach Factory, Raebareli.

q: The first steam locomotive manufactured by the Jamalpur Workshop in 1899, numbered CA 764, was named:
e: CA 764, the first steam locomotive built by the Jamalpur Workshop in 1899, was named Lady Curzon after the wife of the then Viceroy, Lord Curzon.

q: The Rail Spring Karkhana of the North Central Railway, located at Sithouli near Gwalior, mainly manufactures:

options.A: Rail wheels for coaches and wagons
options.D: Hot coil springs for rolling stock

e: The Rail Spring Karkhana at Sithouli near Gwalior, a North Central Railway unit, manufactures hot coil springs used in the suspension of coaches, wagons and locomotives.

q: The Diesel Locomotive Works (DLW) at Varanasi was renamed as the Banaras Locomotive Works (BLW) in the year:
e: Diesel Locomotive Works, Varanasi, was renamed Banaras Locomotive Works in October 2020, reflecting the historic name of the city.

q: The Manduadih railway station in Varanasi was renamed in 2020 as:
e: Manduadih station in Varanasi was renamed Banaras in 2020, restoring the popular traditional name of the city; its station code also changed accordingly.

q: The Rayagada division, created in 2026 by reorganising the erstwhile Waltair division, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The new Rayagada division, formed from 1 June 2026 by reorganising the erstwhile Waltair division, functions under East Coast Railway along with Khurda Road and Sambalpur.

q: The Great Indian Peninsula Railway was merged in 1951 to form which zonal railway?
e: Central Railway was formed on 5 November 1951 by merging the Great Indian Peninsula Railway with the Nizam's, Scindia and Dholpur state railways.

q: The South Coast Railway, notified in 2026 with headquarters at Visakhapatnam, consists of how many divisions?
e: South Coast Railway, headquartered at Visakhapatnam and effective from June 2026, has four divisions - Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Guntur and Guntakal.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'CRS', the statutory authority which inquires into serious railway accidents, stands for:
e: CRS stands for Commissioner of Railway Safety, the statutory authority under the Ministry of Civil Aviation that inspects new lines and inquires into serious railway accidents.

q: In the budgetary cycle of Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'FME', the final review of budget estimates carried out in January, stands for:
e: FME stands for Final Modification Estimates, the second and last budget review in the railway budgetary cycle, carried out in January after the Revised Estimates stage.

q: In railway reservation, the abbreviation 'ARP', the period before the date of journey during which reserved tickets can be booked, stands for:
e: ARP stands for Advance Reservation Period, the window before the journey date during which reserved train tickets can be booked.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'CUG', used for the mobile phone connections provided to railway staff for official communication, stands for:
e: CUG stands for Closed User Group, the mobile service under which railway officials get connections that can call each other within the group for official communication.

q: In railway reservation charts, the waiting list code 'GNWL' stands for:
e: GNWL stands for General Waiting List, the common waiting list for passengers booking from the train's originating station area, which has the best chance of confirmation.

q: In railway operating statistics, the abbreviation 'SFC', which measures the fuel consumed for a specified quantum of traffic, stands for:
e: SFC stands for Specific Fuel Consumption, the fuel consumed per unit of traffic output, used to judge the energy efficiency of locomotive operations.

q: In railway operating statistics, the abbreviation 'GTKM', a measure of the gross load hauled over a distance, stands for:
e: GTKM stands for Gross Tonne Kilometre, the product of the gross weight hauled (including the vehicle) and the distance run, a basic output measure in railway statistics.

q: In stores inventory control on Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'EOQ', the ordering quantity which balances ordering and carrying costs, stands for:
e: EOQ stands for Economic Order Quantity, the order size that minimises the total of ordering cost and inventory carrying cost in stores management.

q: In the maintenance of coaches and locomotives on Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'IOH', an overhaul lighter than the periodic overhaul, stands for:
e: IOH stands for Intermediate Overhaul, a mid-life overhaul of coaches and locomotives that is lighter in scope than the full Periodic Overhaul (POH).

q: In wagon maintenance depots of Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'ROH', the examination and repair given to wagons at fixed intervals, stands for:
e: ROH stands for Routine Overhaul, the periodic examination and repair given to freight wagons in depots at fixed intervals between heavier overhauls.

q: In the Mumbai suburban railway system, the abbreviation 'MUTP', the project under which suburban infrastructure works are executed in phases, stands for:
e: MUTP stands for Mumbai Urban Transport Project, the phased World Bank-assisted programme for improving Mumbai's suburban rail infrastructure and services, executed through MRVC.

q: The capital expenditure allocation (gross budgetary support) for Indian Railways in the Union Budget for 2025-26 was:
e: In the Union Budget 2025-26, Indian Railways received capital expenditure support of Rs 2.52 lakh crore as gross budgetary support, within a total capex plan of Rs 2.65 lakh crore.

q: Indian Railways created a new record by producing how many locomotives in the financial year 2024-25?
e: Indian Railways produced a record 1,681 locomotives in 2024-25, 209 more than the 1,472 of 2023-24, with CLW alone making 700, as per the Ministry of Railways.

q: With a record freight loading in 2024-25, Indian Railways became the second largest freight-carrying railway in the world. The freight loading achieved in that year was:
e: Freight loading rose to 1,617 million tonnes in 2024-25 (about 1,617.38 MT), making Indian Railways the second largest freight-carrying railway in the world.

q: In May 2025, the Prime Minister inaugurated, from Bikaner, how many redeveloped railway stations across the country under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme?
e: In May 2025, the Prime Minister inaugurated 103 redeveloped stations across 18 states and UTs from Bikaner under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.

q: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor, from Ludhiana to Sonnagar, was fully commissioned in the year:
e: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor from Ludhiana (New Sahnewal) to Sonnagar, 1,337 km long, was fully commissioned and ready in October 2023.

q: In June 2025, the Prime Minister flagged off the first export locomotive manufactured at the Marhowra plant in Bihar. The locomotives are being exported to:
e: In June 2025, the Prime Minister flagged off the first export locomotive from the Marhowra plant in Bihar; these Wabtec locomotives are being exported to Guinea for its mining railway.

q: 'Operation AAHT' of the Railway Protection Force is directed mainly against:

options.D: Human trafficking through the railway network

e: Operation AAHT is the RPF's special drive against human trafficking through the railway network, rescuing victims, especially children and women, from trains and stations.

q: The Charlapalli railway terminal, inaugurated in January 2025 as an additional terminal with modern amenities, serves which metropolitan city?
e: The Charlapalli terminal, inaugurated in January 2025 with modern amenities, is an additional coaching terminal serving Hyderabad, easing congestion at Secunderabad and Kacheguda.

q: The 'RailOne' super app launched in July 2025 is the rebranded and upgraded version of the earlier CRIS app named:
e: RailOne is the upgraded successor of SwaRail, the super app launched by CRIS earlier in 2025, integrating reserved and unreserved ticketing, enquiry and grievance services.

q: In May 2025, which State Government became the last among the shareholder States to give its consent for the merger of the Konkan Railway Corporation Limited with Indian Railways?
e: Maharashtra gave its consent in May 2025, the last of the four shareholder states after Goa, Karnataka and Kerala, for merging Konkan Railway with Indian Railways, subject to reimbursement of its equity and retention of the Konkan Railway name.

q: The book 'Ignited Minds', which seeks to inspire the youth of India, was written by:
e: Ignited Minds (2002), dedicated to inspiring India's youth to realise the vision of a developed India, was written by former President A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

q: 'The Story of My Life', the autobiography of a deaf-blind author who became a noted writer and lecturer, was written by:
e: The Story of My Life (1903) is the autobiography of Helen Keller, the deaf-blind American author and lecturer, written with the help of her teacher Anne Sullivan.

q: The book 'How to Win Friends and Influence People', a classic on human relations, was written by:
e: How to Win Friends and Influence People (1936), the classic self-help book on human relations, was written by American author and lecturer Dale Carnegie.

q: The book 'Man's Search for Meaning', based on the author's experiences in Nazi concentration camps, was written by:
e: Man's Search for Meaning (1946) by Viktor Frankl recounts his survival in Nazi concentration camps and presents his logotherapy, based on finding meaning in suffering.

q: The book 'Rich Dad Poor Dad', on personal finance and financial literacy, was written by:
e: Rich Dad Poor Dad (1997), which contrasts the money lessons of two fathers to teach financial literacy and investing, was written by Robert Kiyosaki.

q: The book 'Atomic Habits', on building good habits and breaking bad ones, was written by:
e: Atomic Habits (2018), which teaches building good habits through small incremental changes and breaking bad ones, was written by James Clear.

q: The book 'The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari', a fable about fulfilling one's dreams, was written by:
e: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari (1997), a business fable about a lawyer who seeks spiritual fulfilment in the Himalayas, was written by Robin Sharma.

q: The novel 'The Immortals of Meluha', the first part of the Shiva trilogy, was written by:
e: The Immortals of Meluha (2010), the first book of Amish Tripathi's Shiva Trilogy, retells the story of Shiva as a tribal chief who becomes a saviour.

q: The book 'An Era of Darkness', on the impact of British colonial rule on India, was written by:
e: An Era of Darkness (2016), Shashi Tharoor's critique of the economic and social damage of British colonial rule in India, grew out of his Oxford Union debate speech.

q: The epic poem 'Savitri', based on the Mahabharata tale of Savitri and Satyavan, was composed by:
e: Savitri, the long epic poem in blank verse based on the Mahabharata legend of Savitri and Satyavan, was composed by Sri Aurobindo.

q: The Hindi epic poem 'Rashmirathi', centred on the life of Karna, was written by:
e: Rashmirathi (1952), the celebrated Hindi epic poem on the life and generosity of Karna, was written by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar.

q: The fantasy novel 'The Hobbit', featuring the hobbit Bilbo Baggins, was written by:
e: The Hobbit (1937), the fantasy novel in which Bilbo Baggins journeys with Gandalf and the dwarves to the Lonely Mountain, was written by J. R. R. Tolkien.

q: The political treatise 'The Prince', a classic work on statecraft, was written by:
e: The Prince (written 1513, published 1532), the classic treatise on power and statecraft, was written by the Italian diplomat Niccolo Machiavelli.

q: The Persian epic 'Shahnama' (Book of Kings), one of the longest epic poems of the world, was composed by:
e: The Shahnama, the Persian Book of Kings narrating Iran's mythical and historical past in about 50,000 couplets, was composed by Firdausi.

q: The Hindi novel 'Tamas', set against the Partition of India, was written by:
e: Tamas (1974), the Hindi novel depicting communal violence during the Partition in Punjab, was written by Bhisham Sahni, who also acted in its TV adaptation.

q: The satirical Hindi novel 'Raag Darbari', set in a village of Uttar Pradesh, was written by:
e: Raag Darbari (1968), the satirical Hindi novel set in the fictional village of Shivpalganj in Uttar Pradesh, was written by Shrilal Shukla and won the Sahitya Akademi Award.

q: The ancient Greek epic poem 'The Iliad', centred on the Trojan War, was composed by:
e: The Iliad, the ancient Greek epic on the siege of Troy and the wrath of Achilles, is attributed to the poet Homer.

q: The Task Force on Direct and Indirect Taxes (2002), which recommended wide-ranging tax reforms, was chaired by:
e: The Task Force on Direct and Indirect Taxes (2002), which recommended sweeping reforms to simplify and modernise India's tax system, was chaired by Vijay Kelkar.

q: The J. J. Irani Committee (2005) was set up to recommend reforms in:
e: The J. J. Irani Committee (2005) was constituted to recommend a modern, simplified company law, and its report shaped the later Companies Act reforms.

q: The Kirit Parikh Committee (2013) is associated with recommendations on the pricing of:
e: The Kirit Parikh Committee (2013) recommended a pricing formula for petroleum products, including phased deregulation of diesel and market-linked pricing.

q: The Shyam Benegal Committee (2016) was set up to recommend reforms relating to:
e: The Shyam Benegal Committee (2016) was set up by the Information and Broadcasting Ministry to recommend reforms in film certification by the CBFC.

q: The Committee for the Evolution of the New Education Policy (2016) was chaired by:
e: The Committee for the Evolution of the New Education Policy (2016), which submitted its report before the Kasturirangan drafting committee, was chaired by T. S. R. Subramanian.

q: The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) is associated with recommendations on the development of:
e: The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) recommended measures for the development and promotion of small scale industries, including dereservation and credit reforms.

q: The Deepak Parekh Committee (2007) was set up to recommend measures for the financing of:
e: The Deepak Parekh Committee (2007) on infrastructure financing recommended ways to deepen funding for infrastructure through PPPs, pension and insurance funds and debt markets.

q: The Arvind Subramanian Committee (2015) was set up to recommend the revenue neutral rate and standard rate under the:
e: The Arvind Subramanian Committee (2015) recommended the revenue neutral rate and a standard rate for the Goods and Services Tax, suggesting a standard rate around 17-18 per cent.

q: The N. K. Singh Committee (2016) was set up to review the working of the:
e: The N. K. Singh Committee (2016) was set up to review the FRBM Act and recommended a debt anchor and a fiscal council for better fiscal discipline.

q: The Justice A. P. Shah Committee (2015) was set up to examine the issue of Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) levied on:
e: The Justice A. P. Shah Committee (2015) examined the levy of Minimum Alternate Tax on Foreign Institutional Investors and recommended relief for periods before April 2015.

q: The Sixteenth Finance Commission of India is chaired by:
e: The Sixteenth Finance Commission, constituted for the award period 2026-31, is chaired by economist Arvind Panagariya.

q: Who was the first woman to become the Governor of an Indian State after Independence?
e: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, the first woman to hold the office of Governor of an Indian state after Independence.

q: Which place in Meghalaya is recognised as the wettest place on Earth, receiving the highest average annual rainfall?
e: Mawsynram in Meghalaya's East Khasi Hills receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world, marginally more than nearby Cherrapunji.

q: Who was the first woman to become a Judge of the Supreme Court of India?
e: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, appointed in 1989, was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India and later Governor of Tamil Nadu.

q: The national aquatic animal of India is the:
e: The Ganges river dolphin, found in the Ganga-Brahmaputra river system, was declared India's national aquatic animal in 2009.

q: Who was the first woman to be elected President of the United Nations General Assembly?
e: Vijay Lakshmi Pandit was elected President of the UN General Assembly in 1953, the first woman to hold that post.

q: The Richter scale is used to measure the:
e: The Richter scale measures the magnitude of an earthquake from the energy released, using seismograph recordings.

q: The Indian national flag, in its present form, was designed by:
e: The Indian national flag in its present form, adopted on 22 July 1947, was designed by Pingali Venkayya, with the Ashoka Chakra replacing the charkha.

q: Which is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
e: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake in the world by surface area, covering about 3.71 lakh sq km between Europe and Asia.

q: The first practical typewriter, with the QWERTY keyboard layout, was patented by:
e: Christopher Latham Sholes patented the first practical typewriter in 1868 and devised the QWERTY keyboard layout to prevent typebar jams.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
e: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest, reaching the summit on 23 May 1984.

q: Modern air conditioning, invented in 1902 to control humidity in a printing plant, was developed by:
e: Willis Carrier invented modern air conditioning in 1902 to control temperature and humidity in a Brooklyn printing plant, founding the Carrier Corporation.

q: An audiometer is an instrument used to measure the:
e: An audiometer measures the acuity of hearing by testing a person's ability to hear tones of different frequencies and intensities.

q: The first working laser, built in 1960, was developed by:
e: Theodore Maiman built the first working laser, a ruby laser, in May 1960 at Hughes Research Laboratories.

q: The full form of ENIAC, one of the earliest general-purpose electronic digital computers, is:
e: ENIAC, completed in 1945, stands for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, one of the earliest general-purpose electronic digital computers.

q: The neutron, a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of an atom, was discovered by:
e: The neutron was discovered in 1932 by James Chadwick, who showed that the neutral radiation from beryllium consisted of uncharged particles in the nucleus.

q: The Statue of Liberty in New York was gifted to the United States by:
e: The Statue of Liberty, dedicated in 1886, was a gift from France to the United States to commemorate American independence and Franco-American friendship.

q: The first Cricket World Cup, held in England in 1975, was won by:
e: The first Cricket World Cup, played in England in 1975 as the Prudential Cup, was won by the West Indies, who beat Australia in the final at Lord's.

q: The corporate headquarters of RailTel Corporation of India Limited is located at:
e: RailTel's corporate office is now at East Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi, from where the Navratna telecom PSU runs its nationwide broadband and VPN network.

q: The headquarters of the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) is located at:
e: NHSRCL, the special purpose vehicle executing the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train, has its headquarters in New Delhi.

q: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) is a wholly owned company of the:

options.B: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

e: DFCCIL is a wholly owned company of the Ministry of Railways, created as a special purpose vehicle to build and operate the dedicated freight corridors.

q: In the Railway Energy Management Company Limited (REMCL), the equity is held by RITES Limited and the Ministry of Railways in the ratio of:
e: REMCL is a joint venture in which RITES Limited holds 51 per cent equity and the Ministry of Railways 49 per cent, as recorded in the company's annual report.

q: The Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited (MRVC) was incorporated under the Companies Act in the year:
e: Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Limited was incorporated on 12 July 1999 under the Companies Act to execute the rail component of the Mumbai Urban Transport Project.

q: The administrative control of Burn Standard Company Limited, the wagon-building public sector undertaking, was transferred from the Department of Heavy Industries to the Ministry of Railways in the year:
e: The administrative control of Burn Standard Company Limited was transferred from the Department of Heavy Industries to the Ministry of Railways in 2010.

q: The Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation Limited (IRSDC) was incorporated in the year:
e: IRSDC, set up as a joint venture of RLDA and Ircon to redevelop railway stations, was incorporated in April 2012.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Disaster Management (IRIDM), commissioned in 2019 for hands-on training in railway disaster management, is located at:
e: The Indian Railways Institute of Disaster Management at Bengaluru, commissioned in 2019, gives hands-on training using simulated accident and rescue exercises.

q: The Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya at Vadodara was set up in 2018 as the National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI) with the status of a:
e: The Vadodara institute was set up in 2018 as the National Rail and Transportation Institute with Deemed to be University status, the first such rail-focused university.

q: The National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI) was converted into the Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, a Central University under the Ministry of Railways, in the year:
e: NRTI was converted into Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, a Central University under the Ministry of Railways, by an Act of Parliament in 2022.
